title: Interest Bridge Rate by Credit Line Use — Ridgeline Consumer Credit Rate Table
content:
**Bridge rate.** The interest bridge in a Ridgeline Consumer Credit good-standing amount accrues at the bridge rate, set by how much of the credit line the latest statement balance uses — the latest statement balance divided by the account's credit line (the loan amount on a Ridgeline Project Loan), expressed as a percentage taken to two decimal places:

| Latest statement balance as a share of the credit line | Bridge rate |
|---|---|
| under 25 percent | 6 percent a year |
| at least 25 but under 50 percent | 13.5 percent a year |
| 50 percent or more | the account's purchase APR, as the interest rate schedule shows for its tier |

**Where the rate acts.** The interest bridge is the unpaid minimum multiplied by the bridge rate divided by 100 and by the bridge days, divided by 365 and rounded to the nearest cent.

## Boundary cases (hypothetical credit line 4000.00)

| Latest statement balance | Share of the line | Bridge rate |
|---|---|---|
| 990.00 | 24.75 percent | 6 percent |
| 1000.00 | 25.00 percent | 13.5 percent |
| 1990.00 | 49.75 percent | 13.5 percent |
| 2000.00 | 50.00 percent | purchase APR |

## Hypothetical bridges (unpaid minimum 95.00, 12 bridge days)

At 6 percent: 95.00 multiplied by 6, divided by 100, by 12, divided by 365 — 0.19. At 13.5 percent: 0.42.
